name: Nextmv

modes.label: Native product; see regime notes
modes.note: Standard class 6c9500mb870s (6 cores / 9500 MB / 14.5 min max): 1 credit per second; Innovator PAYG $0.0027/credit = $9.72/h (Scale-up PAYG $6.84/h, prepaid $4.68/$3.24/h). 'Cores' may not equal vCPUs. Premium execution classes (8c16gb12h: 8 cores/16 GB/12 h; 16c60gb12h: 16 cores/60 GB/12 h; amdgpu4c14gb24h: 4 cores/14 GB/24 h + NVIDIA GPU) cost 2 credits/s at a 'Custom' Premium credit rate; must be activated by sales; add 30-60 s runtime overhead. All plans are contact-sales, so the card stays non-priceable.

plans.name: Innovator
plans.note: Contact us; 1 team, 2 users; 600 credits included (=600 standard compute-seconds, $1.62 at PAYG rate); PAYG $0.0027/credit, prepaid $0.0013/credit; 30 runs per day; 15 min per run; Standard compute only; no SSO, no Private deployment.

plans.name: Scale-up
plans.note: Contact us; 1 team, 5 users; 6,000 credits included ($11.40 at PAYG rate); PAYG $0.0019/credit, prepaid $0.0009/credit; 300 runs per day; 15 min per run; Standard compute only.

plans.name: Premium
plans.note: Contact us; 1 team, unlimited users; credits/rates/runs per day all 'Custom'; Premium compute classes (8c16gb12h, 16c60gb12h, amdgpu4c14gb24h) at 2 credits/s; SSO, RBAC, Private deployment, commercial solvers.

caveats: Innovator includes 600 execution credits; paygo $0.0027/credit, prepaid $0.0013. Scale-up 6000 credits; $0.0019/$0.0009. One credit=1 standard compute-second, premium 2 credits/sec. Plan prices quote-led and hardware shape unknown, so per-vCPU rate null.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
Contract overage auto-upgrades: exceeding Order Form limits auto-subscribes the customer to the next tier and fees never automatically decrease.

Default class 'scales horizontally and does not queue requests'; runs above account concurrency are queued per execution class (priority 1-9, default 6) or get HTTP 429 if queuing is disabled. Concurrency numbers unpublished.
Ownership: Nextmv was acquired by FICO (announced 2026-05-19); the product and pricing page are still live (docs footer now '(c) 2026 Fair Isaac Corporation').

fleet.notes: Runs per day: Innovator 30, Scale-up 300, Premium Custom. API: 5 run requests/s, 200 run-result requests per 10 s, 2,000 API requests/min on paid plans (power users 10/s, 500/10 s, 10,000/min on request). Free account: 50 runs lifetime, 30 s max per run. Concurrency still not quantified; over-capacity runs queue per execution class (or 429 if queuing disabled).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Submit a run request with the input (payload) and options (if desired). A run_id is returned.
snapshot_auto.note: Not a machine product: each run is a run-to-completion execution of an app version on an execution class (default 6 cores / 9500 MB / 14.5 min max; premium up to 12-24 h), returning output/assets. No machine state is kept between runs. 'Snapshot' in the docs only refers to app versions (code tags).

snapshot_on_demand.quote: An app version represents a specific executable code. You can think of a version like a Git commit tag. It is a snapshot of the code at a specific point in time.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Versions snapshot pushed code, not a running machine; no checkpoint/restore of runs documented.

harness_api.quote: Use it to manage applications, submit runs, analyze results, and run experiments using natural language in your editor, terminal, or custom agent.
harness_api.note: Nextmv ships a local MCP server (nextmv mcp serve) for external agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code) to drive the platform; no agent harness runs inside Nextmv runs.

ingress_rules.quote: IP Access Control restricts access to your organization to a list of approved IPv4 ranges. The policy applies across all authenticated endpoints, including Nextmv Console and the programmatic API
ingress_rules.note: Runs expose no ports; they are reached only through the authenticated Nextmv API/Console (API keys, SSO, roles). Org-level IPv4 CIDR allowlist (up to 100 rules) is available on request; it does not apply to the session gateway used by custom compute integrations.

secret_proxy.quote: The platform then injects the secrets into the container during the optimization run as environment variables and files.
secret_proxy.note: Secret collections (up to 20 secrets each, type env or file) are placed inside the run; no credential-injecting proxy.

isolation.quote: Runtimes are defined by Docker images. The runtime provides the environment in which the app runs.
isolation.note: Nextmv runs are containerized executions of a submitted app against a fixed set of Nextmv-provided Docker runtime images (execution classes), not a customer-controlled VM/microVM; exact host isolation layer (gVisor/Firecracker/etc.) is undocumented, so 'container' is the best-supported label.

image_oci.quote: Please find the list of available runtimes below. ghcr.io/nextmv-io/runtime/cuopt:latest ... ghcr.io/nextmv-io/runtime/python:3.11
image_oci.note: Customers push app code/binaries to run inside a fixed catalog of Nextmv-published runtime images; there is no documented way to supply your own arbitrary OCI image to run in the cloud.

docker_inside.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps ... Accelerate how you build, test, and deploy scalable decision apps with Nextmv's DecisionOps platform.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Nextmv runs are short-lived optimization/decision executions (run-to-completion, max 15 min-24 h) inside a Nextmv-managed runtime container; no capability to run nested Docker containers is documented.

nested_virt.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a decision-run execution platform, not a VM/hypervisor product; no /dev/kvm or nested virtualization is documented.

desktop.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — an API/CLI-driven decision optimization platform, no graphical desktop is offered.

browser.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser/browser-automation capability is part of the decision-run platform.

computer_use.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no desktop exists to drive via screenshots/clicks.

anti_bot.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser/web-scraping product; anti-bot/stealth features are irrelevant.

captcha_solving.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — an optimization/decision-run API, not a browser/scraping product.

ssh.quote: Learn how to manage applications (create, get, update, delete) with your tool of choice.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — apps are managed via CLI/API/console (push code, submit runs); no SSH access to the execution environment is documented.

snapshot.quote: An app version represents a specific executable code. You can think of a version like a Git commit tag. It is a snapshot of the code at a specific point in time.
snapshot.note: No running-machine snapshot exists; each run is stateless/run-to-completion. 'Snapshot' terminology in docs refers only to app code versions.

fork.quote: An app version represents a specific executable code.
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no machine-cloning concept; only app code versions/instances exist.

fork_running.quote: An app version represents a specific executable code.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no running-machine concept to clone; each run is a stateless one-off execution.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: An app version represents a specific executable code.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no persistent/running machine or memory state to clone.

pause_resume.quote: Submit a run request with the input (payload) and options (if desired). A run_id is returned.
pause_resume.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — runs execute to completion (or timeout) with no pause/resume of an execution.

wake_on_request.quote: Submit a run request with the input (payload) and options (if desired). A run_id is returned.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — each run request provisions a fresh runtime; there is no persistent/sleeping machine to wake.

persistent_disk.quote: Submit a run request with the input (payload) and options (if desired). A run_id is returned.
persistent_disk.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — runs are stateless/ephemeral executions producing output/assets; no persistent machine disk is documented.

volume_attach.quote: Learn how to manage applications (create, get, update, delete) with your tool of choice.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no attachable storage volumes; app code and secrets are the only persisted artifacts.

volume_shared.quote: Learn how to manage applications (create, get, update, delete) with your tool of choice.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shared-volume concept; no persistent machines exist to share storage between.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Submit a run request with the input (payload) and options (if desired). A run_id is returned.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — runs are already stopped automatically at completion/timeout by design (max 15 min on standard, up to 24 h on premium); there is no idle long-lived machine to auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: Premium compute classes (8c16gb12h, 16c60gb12h, amdgpu4c14gb24h) at 2 credits/s
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — CPU/RAM shape is fixed per execution class chosen at run submission; no live resize of a running execution is documented.

agent_harnesses.quote: Use it to manage applications, submit runs, analyze results, and run experiments using natural language in your editor, terminal, or custom agent.
agent_harnesses.note: Nextmv ships a local MCP server so external coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) can drive the Nextmv platform from the user's own machine; no coding-agent harness is preinstalled/offered to run inside a Nextmv execution.

own_agent_api.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Nextmv is a decision-optimization run platform, not a browser/computer-use/research task agent; there is no first-party 'own agent' API of that kind.

lang_python.note: Dedicated Python runtime images (e.g. ghcr.io/nextmv-io/runtime/python:3.11) and a Python SDK are supported out of the box.

lang_node.quote: The main supported languages are: python . Use for Python applications. java . Use for Java applications. binary . Use for compiled applications, such as Go, C, C++, Rust, etc.
lang_node.note: Officially supported app types are python, java, and binary (compiled Go/C/C++/Rust); Node.js/JavaScript is not listed as a supported runtime/SDK.

public_ipv4.quote: Submit a run request with the input (payload) and options (if desired). A run_id is returned.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — runs have no exposed network ports/IPs; they are invoked only via the Nextmv Cloud API/Console.

inbound_https.quote: IP Access Control restricts access to your organization to a list of approved IPv4 ranges. The policy applies across all authenticated endpoints, including Nextmv Console and the programmatic API
inbound_https.note: There is no per-run inbound HTTPS URL to reach a machine; all access goes through the shared, authenticated Nextmv Cloud API/Console endpoint, not a URL exposing the customer's own execution.

egress_http_rules.quote: The platform then injects the secrets into the container during the optimization run as environment variables and files.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented for runs; only account-level inbound IP access control exists.

guest_firewall.quote: Runtimes are defined by Docker images. The runtime provides the environment in which the app runs.
guest_firewall.note: Runs execute in a shared-kernel container runtime, not a full VM/microVM with customer root/kernel access, so guest-level nftables/iptables control is not applicable (root access inside the runtime is not documented either).

static_egress_ip.quote: The platform then injects the secrets into the container during the optimization run as environment variables and files.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP for runs calling external APIs is documented.

windows.quote: ghcr.io/nextmv-io/runtime/default:latest Linux/ARM64 Default runtime for compiled applications such as Go, C++ binaries.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — all documented runtime images are Linux-based; no Windows execution environment exists.

macos.quote: ghcr.io/nextmv-io/runtime/default:latest Linux/ARM64 Default runtime for compiled applications such as Go, C++ binaries.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — only Linux runtime images are documented; no macOS execution environment exists.

arm64.quote: ghcr.io/nextmv-io/runtime/default:latest Linux/ARM64 Default runtime for compiled applications such as Go, C++ binaries.
arm64.note: Most listed runtime images (default, gamspy, java, pyomo, python) are built for Linux/ARM64, indicating ARM64 execution is used for standard runs.

self_host.note: Premium plan offers a sales-negotiated 'Private' deployment option in addition to 'Nextmv Cloud', but this is a vendor-hosted private deployment, not documented as fully self-hostable on arbitrary customer infrastructure without Nextmv.

open_source.quote: Nextmv is the speed and trust layer for all your decision apps
open_source.note: The core DecisionOps platform (Cloud API/Console, run execution) is closed-source/contact-sales SaaS. Nextmv does publish some open-source SDK components (e.g. nextroute at github.com/nextmv-io/nextroute), but that is a solver library, not the platform product itself.
